THIS 6.5-FOOT SPONGE LIVES 2.4 MILES DEEP 

Scientists exploring an unexplored seamount near American Samoa found something enormous hiding in the darkness.

At nearly 3,900 meters below the surface, they discovered a deep-sea sponge standing about 6.5 feet tall.

But the sponge wasn’t alone.

Dead sponge stalks scattered across the seafloor were covered with anemones, barnacles, crinoids and other animals using them as shelter.

Scientists also found a sea star that may represent a previously unknown species.

🌊 What else could be living on this unexplored mountain beneath the Pacific?

SCIENTISTS STILL CAN’T IDENTIFY THIS ANIMAL 
Scientists went nearly 9,100 meters beneath the Pacific Ocean…

And their cameras recorded something they still cannot confidently identify.

The strange animal slowly glided toward the seafloor in the Izu-Ogasawara Trench.

It resembles parts of familiar deep-sea animals—but experts could not assign it to a definite group from the footage.

At these depths, even identifying what you’re looking at can become a scientific mystery.
